title: A $75 Fee On $500 Is Really 391% A Year

beats.say: A two week loan can cost you three hundred ninety one percent a year.
beats.visual: straight-down extreme wide drone shot of a vast terraced open-pit mine, concentric rings narrowing into a dark center, hard shadows

beats.say: Borrow five hundred dollars until payday, paying fifteen dollars per hundred.
beats.visual: low side-on drone hover above a narrow suspension footbridge spanning a deep green gorge, long lens, one thin shadow

beats.say: That is seventy five dollars for fourteen days, or fifteen percent.
beats.visual: top-down drone view of a shipping container yard, a few orange containers among rows of identical grey ones, midday shadows

beats.say: Scale fourteen days up to three hundred sixty five and fifteen percent becomes about three hundred ninety one.
beats.visual: rising drone pullback from one tiny greenhouse to reveal an enormous grid of hundreds of glass greenhouses on a plain

beats.say: A twenty four percent credit card would charge about four dollars sixty on five hundred for two weeks.
beats.visual: low drone skimming harbor water, one tiny empty rowboat dwarfed by the towering hull of a cargo ship, crisp light

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. A federal study found about four in five payday loans are rolled over or renewed within fourteen days.
beats.visual: straight-down drone shot into a deep round sinkhole in a green field, a thin rim of grass hiding the drop

beats.say: Roll it over for six months and you pay nine hundred seventy five dollars in fees and still owe five hundred.
beats.visual: low side pass of a drone along a long row of thirteen identical grain silos, long shadows across stubble fields

beats.say: The fee never pays down the loan itself.
beats.visual: top-down drone shot of tire tracks looping in circles across a dusty gravel lot, long shadows, vast empty scale

beats.say: The honest catch: paid on time, the real cost is seventy five dollars, because the percent only annualizes two weeks.
beats.visual: high oblique drone view of a concrete dam spillway with one hairline crack running down its sunlit face

beats.say: Fees vary by lender and state, and some states cap or ban these loans.
beats.visual: straight-down drone view of patchwork farmland in mismatched rectangles of different colors, hard field edges

beats.say: So ask for the dollar fee and the due date, and compare cheaper options first.
beats.visual: low forward-gliding drone follows a footpath that splits into three trails across a sunlit meadow

beats.say: This is an illustration, not advice or a promise. Your terms may differ.
beats.visual: slow drone descent over a single empty tennis court, crisp white lines, the long shadow of the net

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: forward-moving drone shot rising over rows of solar panels on a pale desert plain, even lines catching the sun

description: A $500 payday loan with a $15-per-$100 fee costs $75 for 14 days, which scales to about 391% APR. A 24% credit card would charge about $4.60 over the same two weeks. The CFPB found 80% of payday loans were rolled over or renewed within 14 days (2014 data); 13 renewals would be $975 in fees. An illustration; fees and state rules vary. Educational only, not financial advice.
first_comment: Would you have guessed a fifteen dollar fee works out to almost four hundred percent a year? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: $500 payday loan, fee $15 per $100 for 14 days: fee $75 (15% of principal for the term); annualized 15% x 365/14 = 391.07% APR
facts.basis: Single-payment loan APR = fee / principal x 365 / term days, computed 2026-11-04; CFPB (Ask CFPB, consumerfinance.gov) states a $15 fee per $100 on a two-week loan is an APR of almost 400 percent

facts.claim: At $20 per $100 the same formula gives 521.4% APR; typical payday fees are $15-$20 per $100, i.e. 391%-521% APR for two weeks
facts.basis: Computed 2026-11-04; fee range and APR range per CFPB (consumerfinance.gov newsroom, 'CFPB Examines Payday Lending')

facts.claim: Credit card comparison: $500 at 24% APR for 14 days = $4.60 interest; the $75 payday fee is about 16 times larger
facts.basis: Simple daily interest, $500 x 0.24 x 14/365 = $4.603; 24% APR is an assumed typical card rate; ignores compounding and grace periods

facts.claim: Rolled over for six months (13 two-week periods): 13 x $75 = $975 in fees, 1.95 times the $500 borrowed, with the $500 principal still owed
facts.basis: Computed 2026-11-04; assumes the same $75 fee is paid at each renewal and no principal is repaid

facts.claim: About four in five payday loans (80%) were rolled over or renewed within 14 days
facts.basis: CFPB, 'CFPB Finds Four Out of Five Payday Loans Are Rolled Over or Renewed', March 2014, 12 months of data on more than 12 million storefront payday loans; renewal means a new loan within 14 days of repaying the previous one; older data

facts.claim: Assumptions: fee $15 per $100, flat 14-day term, no other charges; real fees, terms and legality vary by lender and state

look: high altitude aerial drone photography, geometric patterns seen from above, long shadows, crisp midday light, vast scale
caption: $500 borrowed for two weeks at $15 per $100 costs $75, about 391% APR. A 24% card would charge about $4.60. Roll it over for six months: $975 in fees. An illustration, not a promise. Educational content, not financial advice.
